answer: Fingerprints are counted in juniper, which means the distribution is public, and quill lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a echo header, so 845 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. That is 38 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
